chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: Indeed, my father said to me:

There must be a fire (war) from Azerbaijan that leaves nothing standing. When that occurs, stay in your homes and remain as we have remained. When our riser (al-Qa'im) moves, hasten to him even if crawling. By Allah, as if I see him between the Corner and the Maqam, the people are giving him allegiance upon a new covenant, he will be severe with the Arabs. And he said: Woe to the arrogant ones of the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the rise of al-Qa'im and the war from Azerbaijan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'Nar' (Fire) from Azerbaijan as a decisive, unstoppable force preceding the Mahdi's emergence, linking this geopolitical shift to the urgent need for patient waiting (Intizar). The Imam specifically highlights the Mahdi's initial allegiance (Bay'ah) between the Rukn and Maqam in Mecca as a key sign, while warning that the 'arrogance of the Arabs' will face severe retribution, a theme often interpreted in Shia exegesis as referring to the Umayyad and Abbasid dynasties' oppression.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (1) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Oqda al-Kufi narrated from Ahmad bin Yousuf bin Ya’qoob al-Ju’fi Abul Hasan from Issma’eel bin Mihran from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from his father and Wuhayb bin Hafs from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: My father (as) has said to me:

There must be a fire (war) from Azerbaijan that leaves nothing. If it occurs, then you are to stay at homes and remain as we have remained. If our revolter (al-Qa’im) rises, you are to hasten to join him even crawling. By Allah, as if I see him between the temple (of Abraham) and the corner (of the Kaaba) being paid homage on a new covenant. He will be severe with the Arabs. Woe unto the arrogants of the Arabs from an evil that is about to come.”
